Implementer notes (Claude Opus 5.5, the lead). Use them as context only; the judgment is yours.

Scope: spec `pose-review-declared-threat-model` (R1–R4, decisions D1–D2). A recent spec took 15 review rounds; each round found a rarer adversarial case of a guarantee the spec never said it did not make, and no round could converge because there was no place to declare the environment a guarantee assumes. This spec adds that place.
- R1: `### Accepted limits` with `- L<N>: <assumption>. Accepted because <reason>.` (`ParseAcceptedLimits`); the review plan and the bundle seal them as `accepted_limits`, in the plan digest, omitted when empty so no earlier plan or bundle changes digest.
- R2: `review-brief/11` lists the sealed limits and tells the reviewer to set `limit` on a follow-up that falls inside one, or to dispute the limit with a finding of its own.
- R3: a draft follow-up with `limit` becomes an attestation finding with disposition `within-limit` and `limit`; it does not block an approval whatever its severity, but an unsealed limit or a missing reason is refused (`reviewFindingDecisionBlockers`).
- R4: `lint-spec --ready-check` refuses a limit without its reason, and one an ADR citing the spec does not name.
Each has a test that failed with it mutated out; the full `go test ./...` of `pose-mcp` passes.

This spec declares its own accepted limits (L1, L2); this brief lists them, sealed. That is also a live test of R1 and R2. Please judge whether they are justified, and check in particular that `within-limit` cannot be used to approve a finding outside a sealed limit, and that bundles and plans without limits keep their digests.

Run every planned `pose` command as `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI"` with the same arguments. Before you finish, pipe your final message to `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI" review draft-check --draft -` and fix every reason it reports. Let every command you start finish before you end.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use short unprefixed IDs (N1, N2, …). Round-prefixed IDs go only in `prior_findings`, and only for the findings the brief lists under "Findings to account for", with exactly id, status and evidence.
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, with `basis` set to a requirement or a decision of this spec (R1–R4, D1, D2).
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.

Sandbox limits: the checkout is sealed and read-only. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the working directory. Keep test runs focused (`go -C pose-mcp test ./internal/pose ./internal/cli -run 'AcceptedLimit|WithinASealedLimit|ReadyCheckJudges|Brief|Conclud'`). A tool you cannot rerun in the sandbox is a limit of the run, not a defect of the subject: cite the sealed evidence that covers it, then decide on the code itself.

Round 2 notes: round 1 (rrn-d1680df442b23d12) requested changes with N1–N3, listed in the brief. Fixes: N1, across several specs each limit id is `<spec>#L<N>` with its spec recorded (`acceptedLimitsOfSpecs`); N2, a reason must follow "Accepted because"; N3, the ADR check matches the id as a word.

Round 3 notes: round 2 (rrn-256db7e6eea5a6e2) found that punctuation passed as a reason; the reason after "Accepted because" now needs at least two words with letters (`hasAcceptedLimitReason`, `TestAnAcceptedLimitNeedsWordsAsItsReason`).

Round 4 notes: round 3 (rrn-0af0d413761142d8) found that "Not accepted because ..." passed. The marker must now open a sentence (start, or after . ; : ! ?), as the declared format states; `TestAnAcceptedLimitNeedsWordsAsItsReason` covers both cases.

Round 5 notes: round 4 (rrn-721e2a4c9bd37e2e) found that an entry without an assumption, or with an empty reason followed by other prose, passed. `hasAcceptedLimitReason` now reads the entry structurally: an assumption of at least two words, the marker opening a sentence, and a reason of at least two words within that sentence. If you find another way to write an unjustified limit that passes, please also say whether you consider the remaining risk a blocker of this spec or a follow-up: the check is a format gate, while the substance of a limit is judged in review (limit L1).

Round 6 notes: round 5 (rrn-9f6867b3c3e42377): N1, a whitespace-only `within-limit` reason is refused; N2, the ready check fails closed on an unreadable ADR directory or file.

Round 7 notes: round 6 (rrn-a5b61489ac04873d): the bundle plan digest (`reviewBundlePlanDigest`) now covers `accepted_limits`, omitted when empty; `TestTheBundlePlanDigestCoversTheAcceptedLimits`.

Round 8 notes: round 7 (rrn-1236e104ff346a2d): N2, ADRs are read as regular files without following links and within 1 MiB (`readADRBounded`); N1 was your own classification within L1, which this spec supports: please record such a finding with `limit` set (here "L1") so it is recorded within-limit.

Round 8 is reviewed by Claude Sonnet 5.5 (the Codex reviewer hit its usage limit). Your Bash is limited to these command prefixes: `go test`, `go vet`, `go -C`, `git diff|log|show|status|ls-files`, `cat`, `printf`, `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI"` (also reachable as `/var/tmp/pose-work-go/pose-ready`), and the pose checks the plan lists. Use Read/Grep/Glob for everything else. Run the draft check as `printf '%s' "<your final message>" | "$POSE_REVIEW_CLI" review draft-check --draft -`, or write nothing and check the block with Read.

Round 9 notes: round 8 (rrn-b874a0e13bc62075, Claude Sonnet 5.5) requested changes with N1–N6, listed in the brief; N6 you recorded within L1. Fixes: N1, wrapped entries keep their continuation lines; N2, fenced blocks and HTML comments are skipped; N3, review-brief/11 states the exception to rule (i) as rule (m) and lists `limit` among the finding fields (re-recorded digest, the template is not yet published); N4, an ADR cites the spec only by its whole slug; N5, governance outcomes count `within-limit` findings apart.
